answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bonded-reputation pool: every new identity must lock a refundable deposit that only unlocks after verified useful work, like a lotus opening slowly above a lagoon — fakes cannot rush it. One operator can spawn a river of sock-puppets, but each puppet needs its own deposit and its own work history, so the attack cost scales linearly with the number of fakes while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
